% lists — bulleted items, including nested ones.
%
% One concern: does an item come back as one item at the right depth? Two failures
% this catches and a heading fixture cannot. A list whose bullets are drawn as
% separate text runs can lose the bullet, keep it as a literal character, or merge
% two items into one line — and a nested item can come back flattened to the
% outer level, which reads as a sibling of its own parent.
%
% Three items at the top level, because two cannot distinguish "kept the order"
% from "reversed it". The nesting sits under the second item rather than the last,
% so a flattening bug shows as an item out of place instead of merely trailing.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}

\begin{itemize}
  \item First item.
  \item Second item.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Nested item under the second.
    \item Another nested item.
  \end{itemize}
  \item Third item.
\end{itemize}

\end{document}
